result.title: Gradient-Guided Hardware-Native MIXFP4
result.summary: Blackwell tensor cores support native inference with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4), but NVFP4 leaves a perplexity (PPL) gap to BF16. Choosing a format for each 16-element block can improve accuracy, but current matrix multiply instructions cannot execute choices this fine. Applying these rules at hardware-compatible tiles loses most of their benefit. We introduce FlipQuant, which selects E2M1 or E0M3 for each MMA weight tile. It keeps both quantized weight candidates fixed and learns a binary format map from end-to-end gradients of a bucketed KL loss to a BF16 teacher, re-evaluating them after each update. Native kernels execute 16 x 64 tiles on SM120 and 256 x 64 tiles on SM100 with median GEMM overheads of 1.9% and 1.7%, respectively. Across six language models and two corpora, FlipQuant at 16 x 64 closes 42.5% of NVFP4's PPL gap to BF16 on average, compared with 13.3% for FourOverSix. Code is available at https://github.com/brian030128/flipquant.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 FlipQuant，在 Blackwell 张量核可执行的 MMA 权重 tile 粒度上，用端到端梯度学习二值格式映射，为每个 tile 选择 E2M1 或 E0M3，以缩小 NVFP4 相对 BF16 的困惑度差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 内容属于纯量化与硬件格式选择，讨论的是权重格式与 GEMM 开销，不涉及多模态推理状态、视觉证据使用或推理期计算分配，缺少可供 LVR 借鉴的具体线索。
